This enables a two-stage KernelSU + ReZygisk process.
Stage 1: • The app runs the normal exploit and late-loads KernelSU. • It does not touch the zygote or start the ReZygisk monitor yet. • When KernelSU is active, the app asks you to close it and open KernelSU.
Stage 2: • Grant Root My Galaxy superuser access in KernelSU. • Return to Root My Galaxy. The home card will change to “KernelSU active — ReZygisk ready”. • Tap the card to start the monitor, schedule the controlled zygote restart, verify injection and system_server, or roll back on failure.
Before starting: 1. Install and enable ReZygisk in KernelSU. 2. Remove or disable NeoZygisk, Zygisk Next, BreZygisk, and every other Zygisk provider. 3. For the first test, disable Vector, TreatWheel, NoHello, and all other Zygisk modules. 4. Do not run post-fs-data scripts manually and do not perform a soft reboot yourself.
A full watchdog reboot is still possible during the injection stage and would remove runtime root.

The exploit stage is complete. Close Root My Galaxy completely, open KernelSU, grant Root My Galaxy superuser access, and return to Root My Galaxy. The home card will then let you start the ReZygisk process.
